newsitem.title: USA: EPA overestimated health benefit of clean air plan.
newsitem.headline: EPA overestimated health benefit of clean air plan.

text.p: The U.S. Environmental Protection Agency said on Wednesday it had overestimated by one-third the number of deaths it would prevent by tightening clean air standards.
Correcting conclusions from its data, the agency said stricter limits on smog and soot would prevent about 15,000 premature deaths, down from the 20,000 it had orginally estimated.
"EPA is continuing to refine this estimate," EPA assistant administrator Mary Nichol said in a statement.
Industry groups, concerned that new emissions limits would be extremely costly to meet, have raised numerous questions about the science used to justify the tighter limits.
The new error was brought to the agency's attention by an independent consultant, agency officials said.
"Clearly, this (public comment) process is working and is vital to ensuring that the final air quality standards are based on the best available science and protect the public health," Nichols said.
